Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt

many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Use this procedure when handling a puzzle in a Continual-ARC stream.

3. Run the transform on every received input/output pair. Preserve each demo as the complete grid as received and compare complete returned grids exactly; do not substitute a sparse reconstruction or hand-derived expected output, since fixture transcription errors can masquerade as rule failures. After each code edit, rerun every pair; an exception or mismatch means the program is not validated, so do not submit yet. Once all pairs match, run it on the test grid and submit only that returned grid. Keep one action JSON object as the last line of every puzzle reply.
4. After a submission verdict, replace the task file with the version that reproduces all available demos, then finish only when the instance is over. Do not claim a task-specific rule is reusable unless it is supported by evidence beyond that instance.

from collections import Counter

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    bg = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    pts = [(r, c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] != bg]
    if not pts:
        return [row[:] for row in grid]
    r0, r1 = min(r for r, c in pts), max(r for r, c in pts)
    c0, c1 = min(c for r, c in pts), max(c for r, c in pts)
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    for c in range(c0, c1 + 1):
        if out[r0][c] == bg: out[r0][c] = 2
        if out[r1][c] == bg: out[r1][c] = 2
    for r in range(r0, r1 + 1):
        if out[r][c0] == bg: out[r][c0] = 2
        if out[r][c1] == bg: out[r][c1] = 2
    return out
